axes.solve: prior-anchored ridge on w2, lambda ladder to update_scale<=1.0, arm=conditioned-local

heldout.note: a deleted block has no local write to score

axes.solve: absorbed by every downstream conditioned solve

axes.evidence: the sealed corpus, for a token OCCURRENCE census only; no activation, no capture, no forward pass
axes.heldout: not applicable: nothing is fitted.  What IS measured out of sample is the segmentation shift -- position agreement 0.2918 on the sealed corpus and 0.0399 on the frozen review prompts, with tokens-per-byte beside it
axes.selection: the 5120 rows kept by: every added/special token and every one of the 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens (mandatory -- byte_fallback is false and there is no unk, so those 256 are the only reason an arbitrary byte can still be encoded), the transitive merge-tree closure of everything kept, and then the ranking (-census count, parent token id) until the budget is exactly met.  The census sums two streams over the sealed corpus: the donor-mapped ids the captures ran on and this tokenizer's own canonical segmentation of the same text.  With only 3027 observed tokens admitted beyond the mandatory set, the tie-break -- parent id order, which for a BPE table is its merge order and therefore its training-corpus frequency order -- decides most of this table, and that is stated rather than implied
axes.solve: NONE.  The rows are gathered verbatim; the identity gate is torch.equal against the source table's own bytes, not a tolerance.  The merge list is restricted to the closure (a merge survives iff its product and both operands are kept) and the ids are densely remapped, including the TemplateProcessing special-token ids, which carry hard ids a remap that missed them would silently corrupt

calibration.inapplicable_reason: A standard-shape child has no copy-exact reproduction gate: the gate multiplies held-out input rows by ONE parent weight and compares them to that tensor's own output, and this child replaces no parent tensor shape-for-shape.  The parent itself is the only copy-exact control a shape change has, and it is used as such in the composed block below.
